# Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric extends Consul service mesh governance to AI
agents, so that their calls to large language models (LLMs), other agents, and
Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools travel over authenticated, policy-controlled
paths.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric components run in the Consul control plane and data plane, while applications and external systems keep responsibility for planning, business logic, and user identity.

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Introduction

An AI application can call a model, delegate work to another agent, and invoke tools on behalf of a user. Each interaction requires a distinct decision: whether the workload can connect, whether the user has delegated authority, whether the requested model or tool is permitted, and whether the operation requires human approval.

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric separates these decisions across gateways, identity integrations, application-local development libraries, and observability components. Consul workload identity and service intentions remain the foundation for mesh connectivity. They do not replace delegated user authorization or application policy.

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric builds on Consul service registration, workload identity, service intentions, and proxy configuration. These mechanisms establish governed network paths. Additional processors interpret model and tool requests, integrate delegated user authority, and apply component-specific policy.

An AI application remains responsible for planning work, choosing operations, and interpreting results. Network authorization does not establish that an operation is appropriate for a user's task or that a successful response meets the application's requirements.

## Components

| Component | Responsibility | Architectural boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [AI Inference Gateway](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/inference-gateway) | Govern model access, routing, provider translation, usage controls, and data protection. | Honor-permitted explicit model choices and caller-approved fallback. |
| [MCP sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/mcp-sidecar) | Govern Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool discovery and invocation. | Catalog visibility does not grant permission to invoke a tool. Backends own tool business logic. |
| [Identity plane](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity) | Carry destination-scoped delegated user authority alongside workload identity. | Customer identity and access management (IAM) remains the token issuer. |
| [External credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection) | Authenticate approved external HTTP MCP and API calls at the terminating gateway. | Callers cannot choose secret locations or override trusted destination bindings. |
| [AI observability](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability) | Correlate operational signals, model attribution, and audit requirements. | Telemetry delivery and content capture require explicit controls; traces alone are not a complete audit ledger. |
| [Auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation) | Automatically instrument supported model and tool traffic and supply inputs for operational metrics and business KPIs. | No application tracing SDK is required; applications preserve trace context and supply business outcomes that proxies cannot establish. |
| [Cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection) | Use Agentic Analytics findings to open agent-scoped circuits for unproductive repetition. | Repeated arguments alone do not prove a cycle; asynchronous enforcement cannot undo completed actions. |

For the architectural layers and how these components work together, refer to [Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric architecture](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/architecture).

## Get started
